---
title: "UVP Lipids and morphotraits analysis"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-01-21"
output: html_document
---

This is the preliminary exploration of the contents of the UVP5 and UVP6 copepod data. The morphological traits estimated within ecotaxa are analyzed with the metadata. The prosome and lipid content segmented as the training dataset and as the result of the fastai image segmentation pipeline are additionally used as trait information.

Data preparation tasks:
1. Load the UVP5/6 metadata file that include the morphological traits.
2. Based on the file of image masks, label which images have prosome and lipid masks.
3. For the manually segmented images, get the number of pixels assigned prosome or lipid and convert to mg.
4. For the ML segmented imaged, get number of pixels assigned prosome or lipid and convert to mg. 
5. Also calculate the major axis and minor axis lengths of the segmented prosome and lipids.

(3-5 might be done in Python when processing the ML segmentation results)


Data analysis tasks:
A. Sampling information
- open TSV files and filter columns
- visualize the spatial 3D and temporal distribution of the image data
- classify images according to depth or environmental zones

B. Segmentation model accuracy
- compare the pixels and mg differences between the manual and ML segmentations
- make sure to separate which images were used as training or test data


C. Morphological traits
- do ordinations and similar analysis as with Laure's UVP5 greenedge analysis
- estimate lipid content from biovolume using published allometric scaling relationships

D. Prosome size and lipid traits
- scaling relationship between prosome and lipid content, by area and by length
- plot the spatial distribution of the lipid content


E. Lipid content and morphological traits
- compare the major and minor axis lengths (and resulting biovolume) of the segmented images with that of the ecotaxa morphotraits
- find correlations between morphotraits and lipid content
- find relationships between morphotraits and if an image has a segmented (visible) lipid sac. I.e. are there predictors for these based on the ecotaxa data
- project the prosome and lipid content traits against the ordination of the morphological traits

# Load data and libraries

Important: LOKI metadata does not include longitude and latitude. This could be extracted by matching the files from arcticnet2013 ecotaxa projects

! The arcticenet2015 loki images are not yet in

Note that images here only copepods labelled with visible lipids.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
#devtools::install_github("jiho/morphr", force =T)
# library("morphr")

source("../Vilgrain2021/lib/kaiser_guttman.R")
theme_set(theme_bw())

uvp5_ge_side <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP5_greenedge/ecotaxa_export_149_20241018_1551.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp5_ge_top <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP5_greenedge/ecotaxa_export_149_20241018_1553.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp5_ge <- bind_rows(uvp5_ge_side, uvp5_ge_top)
rm(uvp5_ge_side, uvp5_ge_top)


uvp6_de_side <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1521.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp6_de_top <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1518.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
uvp6_de <- bind_rows(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top)
rm(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top)

# Only "Calanus" so far
uvp6_amund <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_amundsen2023/Calanus/ecotaxa_export_10101_20250117_1943.tsv",sep = '\t', header = TRUE)
# filter columns?

# Only copepods with visible lipid sac
loki <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/LOKI_for_prosome_segmentation/ecotaxa_export_2331_20241009_1551.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE)



# Column names are not exactly the same for all files. Determine which metadata is found in each file
meta <- data.frame(instrument = "uvp5_ge",
                   cnames = colnames(uvp5_ge)) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "uvp6_de",
                   cnames = colnames(uvp6_de))) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "uvp6_amund",
                       cnames = colnames(uvp6_amund))) %>% 
  bind_rows(data.frame(instrument = "loki",
                       cnames = colnames(loki))) %>%
  
  # Create a wide table of column names and corresponding datasets
  mutate(iscol = 1) %>% 
  group_by(cnames) %>% 
  mutate(ndata = sum(iscol)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = instrument, values_from = iscol, values_fill = NA) %>% 
  arrange(-ndata)

meta.all <- meta %>% 
  filter(ndata == max(ndata))

meta.uvp <- meta %>% 
  filter(ndata >= 3) %>% 
  filter(uvp6_amund == 1)


# LOKI2013 an UVP6_DE annotated and predicted prosome and lipid results
prosome_uvp6 <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_uvp6deamund_prosome.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
lipid_uvp6 <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_uvp6deamund_lipid.csv",
                         header = TRUE)

prosome_loki <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_loki2013_prosome.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
lipid_loki <- read.csv("data/prediction_results_loki2013_lipid.csv",
                         header = TRUE)
```

# Explore the morphospace from the UVP data

18 Morphological descriptors (Gorsky et al. 2010)
Size	Major = primary axis of an ellipse fitted on the object
	Minor = secondary axis of an ellipse fitted on the object
	Area = object area (i.e. number of pixels belonging to the object)
	Feret = distance between the 2 further points along object’s perimeter
	Perim. = perimeter length of the object
Shape	Circ. = circularity measure = (4*π*area)/perim., 1 = circle, 0 = line.
	Elongation = major/minor, 1 = circular >1 = elongated
	Thickr = Thickness ratio, relation between the maximum thickness of an object and the average thickness of the object excluding the maximum (Romagnan et al. 2016)
	Ver.Sym. = bilateral symmetry index
	Ver.Sym.2 = bilateral symmetry index taking into account only 75% of the darker pixels)
Transparency	Mean.grey = average grey value within the object ; sum of the grey values of all pixels in the object divided by the number of pixels (low = dark objects, high = clear objects)
	Med.grey = median grey value within the object
	Hist.grey 75% = grey level value at 75% of the normalized cumulative histogram of grey levels
	Sdev.grey = standard deviation of the grey value used to generate the mean grey value
	Skew.grey = skewness of the histogram of grey level values
Complexity	Perim./Major = Refers to both complexity (high values if the perimeter is particularly complex for an object of a given size) and circularity (round objects have a high perimeter/diameter ratio).
	Perim./Feret = same interpretation
	Fractal = fractal dimension of perimeter (Bérubé and Jébrak 1999)


```{r}
uvp.img <- uvp5_ge %>% 
  select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
  mutate(instrument = "uvp5_ge") %>% 
  bind_rows(uvp6_de %>% 
              select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
              mutate(instrument = "uvp6_de") ) %>% 
  bind_rows(uvp6_amund %>% 
              select(meta.uvp$cnames) %>% 
              mutate(instrument = "uvp6_amund") ) %>% 
  relocate(instrument) %>% 
  distinct(object_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Subset of metadata information, columns renamed
uvp.meta <- uvp.img %>% 
  select(object_id, instrument,
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         annotation = object_annotation_category, sample_id, sample_cruise)

# Zooprocess morphological descriptors
# 18 traits were used in the Vilgrain et al. (2021) analysis
# zf <- select(z, Major, Minor, Perim., Feret, Area, Elongation ,
#              Ver.Sym., Ver.Sym.2, Circ., Thickr , Mean.grey, Med.grey,
#              "Hist.grey 75%", Sdev.grey, Skew.grey, Fractal,
#              "Perim./Feret", "Perim./Major")

uvp.morpho <- uvp.img %>% 
  select(object_id,
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, Perim. = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
         Ver.Sym. = object_symetriev, Ver.Sym.2 = object_symetrievc, 
         Circ. = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         Mean.grey = object_mean, Med.grey = object_median,
         `Hist.grey 75%` = object_histcum3, 
         Sdev.grey = object_stddev, Skew.grey = object_skew,
         Fractal = object_fractal, 
         `Perim./Feret` = object_perimferet,
         `Perim./Major` = object_perimmajor) %>% 
  remove_rownames() %>% 
  column_to_rownames("object_id")


pca <- FactoMineR::PCA(as.matrix(uvp.morpho), graph = FALSE)
# Note can weigh rows based on concentration

plot(pca, label = "var")
plot(pca, choix="var", axes = c(1,2))
plot(pca, choix="var", axes = c(3,4))

summary(pca)

# selection of axis :
kaiser_guttman(pca)


```

# Relate accuracy of CNN with morphospace
Difference in values is annotated - predicted. So + values mean that the model underestimated.
```{r}
uvp6_accuracy_prosome <- prosome_uvp6 %>% 
  mutate(prosome_pixels_diff = prosome_pixels_annotated - prosome_pixels_predicted,
         prosome_mass_diff = prosome_mass_annotated - prosome_mass_predicted) %>% 
  rename(prosome_iou = IoU, prosome_recall = Recall, prosome_f1score = F1score) 
  # select(directory, filename, prosome_pixels_diff, prosome_mass_diff,
  #        prosome_iou, prosome_recall, prosome_f1score)

uvp6_accuracy_lipid <- lipid_uvp6 %>% 
  mutate(lipid_pixels_diff = lipid_pixels_annotated - lipid_pixels_predicted,
         lipid_mass_diff = lipid_mass_annotated - lipid_mass_predicted) %>% 
  rename(lipid_iou = IoU, lipid_recall = Recall, lipid_f1score = F1score) 
  # select(directory, filename, lipid_pixels_diff, lipid_mass_diff,
  #        lipid_iou, lipid_recall, lipid_f1score)
  
uvp6_accuracy <- left_join(uvp6_accuracy_prosome, uvp6_accuracy_lipid,
                           by = "filename") %>% 
  
  filter(!is.na(lipid_pixels_diff)) %>%  # only images with lipid annotations
  # calculate lipid fullness 
  mutate(lipidfullness_pixels_annotated = lipid_pixels_annotated / 
           prosome_pixels_annotated * 100) %>% 
  mutate(lipidfullness_pixels_predicted = lipid_pixels_predicted / 
           prosome_pixels_predicted * 100) %>% 
  mutate(lipidfullness_mass_annotated = lipid_mass_annotated / 
           prosome_mass_annotated * 100) %>% 
  mutate(lipidfullness_mass_predicted = lipid_mass_predicted / 
           prosome_mass_predicted * 100) %>%
  mutate(lf_pixels_diff = lipidfullness_pixels_annotated -
           lipidfullness_pixels_predicted,
         lf_mass_diff = lipidfullness_mass_annotated -
           lipidfullness_mass_predicted) %>% 
  
  # remove the raw values, only retain differences
  select(-c(prosome_pixels_annotated, prosome_pixels_predicted,
            prosome_mass_annotated, prosome_mass_predicted,
            lipid_pixels_annotated, lipid_pixels_predicted,
            lipid_mass_annotated, lipid_mass_predicted,
            lipidfullness_pixels_annotated, lipidfullness_pixels_predicted,
            lipidfullness_mass_annotated, lipidfullness_mass_predicted,
            directory.x, directory.y)) %>% 
  
  # create object_id column to match the ecotaxa export data
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png")) %>% 
  
  # TODO filter model performance quality
  # sometimes the segmentation model fails of very bad
  filter(is.finite(lf_mass_diff)) %>%
  filter(lf_mass_diff >= -100)

rm(uvp6_accuracy_prosome, uvp6_accuracy_lipid)

ggplot(uvp6_accuracy) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x = lf_pixels_diff))
  

# subset of the ecotaxa export data with adjusted column names
# NOTE slightly changed variable names
uvp6_de_sub <- bind_rows(uvp6_de, uvp6_amund) %>% 
  # sometimes the ecotaxa output can be doubled each for the white and black bg images
  distinct(object_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  select(object_id, 
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         annotation = object_annotation_category, sample_id, sample_cruise,
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, Perim = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
         VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
         Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         Meangrey = object_mean, Medgrey = object_median,
         Histgrey75 = object_histcum3, 
         Sdevgrey = object_stddev, Skewgrey = object_skew,
         Fractal = object_fractal, 
         Perim.Feret = object_perimferet,
         Perim.Major = object_perimmajor) 

# add morphotrait information
uvp6_accuracy <- uvp6_accuracy %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_de_sub, by = "object_id")


# check some patterns
ggplot(uvp6_accuracy, aes(x = lipid_iou, y = Perim)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = depth)) +
  geom_smooth()

ggplot(uvp6_accuracy, aes(x = lf_mass_diff, y = Perim)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = depth)) +
  geom_smooth()


ggplot(uvp6_accuracy, aes(x = prosome_pixels_diff, y = Area)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Elongation)) +
  geom_smooth()
```

## TODO Characteristics of model accuracy
### 1. Basic regression 
test to check if any of the morphological traits are strong predictors of segmentation model accuracy - no clear linear trends
```{r}
reg.models <- expand.grid(X = colnames(uvp6_accuracy[2:13]),
                          Y = colnames(uvp6_accuracy[23:40]),
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>% 
  mutate(base = "none")

reg.results <- data.frame()
for (i in c(1:nrow(reg.models))){
  reg.results <- bind_rows(reg.results, 
                           getRegressionModel(uvp6_accuracy, 
                                              reg.models$X[i], reg.models$Y[i],
                                              base = reg.models$base[i]))
}
```

### 2. Exploratory ordination

#### biplot function
```{r}
'p_biplot_pca_points' <- 
  function(rdaoutput, xmat = NULL, cluster, axestoplot=c(1,2), 
           legendtitle = 'Groups', plottitle = NULL, 
           standardizeXmat = TRUE, alpha = 0.8, ellipse.conf = 0.8,
           clrs = brewer.pal(9, "Set1"), 
           rescaleSites = 1, scaleCorrelations = FALSE) {
    require(RColorBrewer)
    require(ggrepel)

    # axismat <- rdaoutput$CA$u
    axismat <- vegan::scores(rdaoutput, choices = axestoplot, display = "sites")
    varexp <- round( rdaoutput$CA$eig/rdaoutput$tot.chi*100, digits = 1)
    
    # Change axis names to contain % variance explained
    axisname <-  colnames(axismat) 
    a1 <- axisname[1]
    a2 <- axisname[2]
    
    
    # Rescale the site scores to highlight the arrows in the biplot
    axismat.rescaled <- axismat * rescaleSites
    
    
    g <- ggplot(as.data.frame(axismat.rescaled), 
                aes_string(axisname[1],axisname[2], colour = cluster)) + 
      labs(x = paste0(a1," (",varexp[axestoplot[1]],"%)"), 
           y = paste0(a2, " (",varexp[axestoplot[2]], "%)" )) +
      geom_point(size = 3, alpha = alpha, shape = 16, aes(colour=cluster))  + 
      stat_ellipse(size = 1.5,show.legend = FALSE,level = ellipse.conf) +
      geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour='darkgray') + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour='darkgray') +
      theme_bw() +
      theme(legend.position="none", 
            # legend.background = element_rect(colour="gray", size=0.5, linetype="solid"),
            legend.title = element_text(color = 'black', size = 12, face = 'bold'),
            legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
            aspect.ratio = 1) 
      # ggtitle(plottitle)
    
    if (is.factor(cluster) == TRUE)  { 
      g <- g + scale_color_manual(values = clrs, name = legendtitle)#+scale_color_brewer(palette="Set1")
    } else { 
      g <- g + scale_colour_continuous(name = legendtitle)
    }
    
    # Project standardized explanatory variables to PCoA axes
    if (is.null(xmat) == FALSE) {
      if (standardizeXmat == TRUE) {
        xmat = scale(xmat , center=TRUE, scale=TRUE)
      } 
      n <- nrow(xmat)
      points.stand <- scale(axismat)
      
      # Predictors appear as correlations
      U <- cor(xmat, points.stand, use="pairwise.complete.obs")  # pairwise to disregard NAs for variables with blanks
      
      if (scaleCorrelations == TRUE) {
        maxpos <-  min(max(abs(axismat[,1])),max(abs(axismat[,2])))# previously = 1
      } else {
        maxpos <- c(1,1)
      }
      
      Udf <- data.frame(x1 = rep(0,nrow(U)),y1 =rep(0,nrow(U)), xend = U[,1]*maxpos, yend = U[,2]*maxpos)
      g <- g + 
        geom_point(data = Udf, aes(x = xend, y = yend),
                   color = "black", size = 2) +
        # geom_segment(data = Udf, aes(x = x1, y = y1, xend = xend, yend = yend),
        #              lineend = "round", size = 0.5, colour = "grey40") +
        ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = Udf, aes(x = xend, y = yend, label=rownames(U)), 
                        color="black", size = 4) 
    }
    
    plot(g)
  }

```

# Random forest model of lipid estimation from morphotraits
Applying a random forest model using the morphological traits to predict lipid mass (%var exp = 88%) and prosome mass (% var exp = 95%) are not that bad. RF model for lipid fullness based on mass is at %var exp = 96.3%.

But RF model for lipid fullness based on pixels is awful at %var exp = 6% and LF based on mass at 5.5%. Wonder why the latter is performs badly. Both prosome and lipid mass have a nonlinear relationship to lipid fullness. 


Running the random forest models without Depth as a predictor does not affect the performance for lipid and prosome mass but it actually makes the lipid fullness RF model weaker with (% var exp = 2.6%) indicating that depth is likely an important predictor of fullness, even if these two variables do not have a clear relationship when doing a correlation. Interestingly, including lipid and prosome mass as predictors for the lipid fullness RF model increases the %var expl to 61% which means that the morpho traits could potentially predict for LF but doesn't in this RF model. This is probably simulated with a neural network instead?

## The function getRegressionModel2 from lmodel2 allows for reduced major axis regression but here OLS is used.
```{r}
# Calculates regression model using the lmodel2() function that allows major axis regressions
# df is a standardized trait dataframe
getRegressionModel2 <- function(df, grp = "All", X, Y, 
                               model = "OLS", base = "10"){
  trait.sub <- df
  if (grp != "All") {
    trait.sub <- trait.sub %>% 
      filter(str_detect(group, grp)) 
  }
  trait.sub <- trait.sub %>% 
    filter(!is.na(get(X)) & !is.na(get(Y))) %>% 
    relocate(X, Y)
  
  # This calculates both the OLS and RMA
  if(base == "10") {
    reg <- lmodel2::lmodel2(log10(get(Y)) ~ log10(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
  } else if (base == "e") {
    reg <- lmodel2::lmodel2(log(get(Y)) ~ log(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
  } else {
    stop("Error: Please select either base 10 or e.")
  }

  if (model == "OLS"){
    ii <- 1
  } else if (model =="RMA") {
    ii <- 3
  } else {
    stop("Error: Please select either OLS or RMA regression model.")
  }
  
  # return(reg)
  
  reg.results.size <- data.frame(grp = grp, X = X,  Y = Y, 
                                 a = reg$regression.results$Intercept[ii], 
                                 b = reg$regression.results$Slope[ii], 
                                 a.ci.2.5 = reg$confidence.intervals$`2.5%-Intercept`[ii],
                                 a.ci.97.5 = reg$confidence.intervals$`97.5%-Intercept`[ii],
                                 b.ci.2.5 = reg$confidence.intervals$`2.5%-Slope`[ii],
                                 b.ci.97.5 = reg$confidence.intervals$`97.5%-Slope`[ii],
                                 n = nrow(trait.sub), 
                                 R2 = reg$rsquare,
                                 # RSE = reg$sigma,
                                 pval = reg$P.param, 
                                 model = model, base = as.character(base),
                                 minX = min(trait.sub[,1]), maxX = max(trait.sub[,1]))
}

# OLS regression model function

getRegressionModel <- function(df, X, Y, base = "10") {
  trait.sub <- df %>% 
    filter(!is.na(get(X)) & !is.na(get(Y))) %>% 
    relocate(X, Y)
  
  if (nrow(trait.sub) > 3) {
    # Calculate OLS
    if(base == "10") {
      reg <- lm(log10(get(Y)) ~ log10(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "e") {
      reg <- lm(log(get(Y)) ~ log(get(X)), data = trait.sub)
    } else if (base == "none") {
      reg <- lm(get(Y) ~ get(X), data = trait.sub)
    } else {
      stop("Error: Please select either base 10, e, or none.")
    }
    
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = reg$coefficients[1],
                              b = reg$coefficients[2],
                              n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = summary(reg)$adj.r.squared,
                              RSE = summary(reg)$sigma,
                              pval = getpval(summary(reg)$fstatistic), 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = min(trait.sub[,1]), maxX = max(trait.sub[,1]))
  } else {
    reg.results <- data.frame(X = X,  Y = Y, 
                              a = NA, b = NA, n = nrow(trait.sub),
                              R2 = NA, RSE = NA, pval = NA, 
                              model = "OLS", base = as.character(base),
                              minX = NA, maxX = NA)
  }
  
  return(reg.results %>% 
           remove_rownames())
}

getpval <- function(x){ 
  p <- pf(x[1],x[2],x[3],lower.tail = F) 
  attributes(p) <- NULL
  return(p)
}

```

The OLS models have R2 ranging from 0.64-0.88. Best models use area to predict for prosome mass (R2 = 0.88) and lipid mass (R2 = 0.81). So the random forest models result in better models based on higher R2.
